payload.body:
## Context
Linear OAuth, connection persistence, and webhook delivery storage are now live in auth-broker. The broker currently exposes `/v1/auth/linear/connections` and `/v1/auth/linear/deliveries*` without a real authenticated user/team access model.

## Goals
- Define and implement the auth model for broker-side Linear routes.
- Scope connection and delivery visibility by Better Auth user and org/team membership.
- Prevent unauthenticated listing or mutation of connected account metadata and pending webhook deliveries.

## Notes
- Current provider metadata explicitly reports `accessControlMode: manual_unenforced`.
- Linear callback now links Better Auth users by email and persists `betterAuthUserId`, so the next step is enforcement, not more identity capture.
- Consider whether local clients should use Better Auth sessions, broker-issued device claims, or signed service tokens.

## Links
- services/auth-broker/src/modules/linear-connections/plugin.ts
- services/auth-broker/src/modules/linear-sync-store/plugin.ts
- services/auth-broker/src/modules/linear-oauth/service.ts

payload.body:
## Context
Linear OAuth, connection persistence, pending webhook deliveries, and Better Auth user/org scoping are now live in `auth-broker`, and unauthenticated access to connection/delivery routes is blocked.

## Goals
- Finish the remaining access-control work by enforcing team-scoped visibility and mutation rules for Linear connection and delivery routes.
- Preserve legacy fallback behavior for user-owned and org-owned records created before team ownership is first-class.
- Make provider/access metadata accurately report the strongest active Better Auth scope.

## Notes
- This ticket now covers the remaining team-authz gap only; user/org scoping is already shipped.
- Depends on first-class ownership persistence so team ownership is queryable without JSON-envelope fallbacks.

## Context
Manual-first Linear sync is shipped and the phase-3 autosync design is now documented.

## Goals
- Capture the completed autosync design and hand implementation to the new execution ticket.

## Notes
- Design completed in:
  - `docs/plans/2026-03-06-linear-phase-3-completion-design.md`
  - `docs/plans/2026-03-06-linear-phase-3-completion-plan.md`
- Implementation follow-up is tracked separately in the new autosync execution ticket created from this plan.

## Links
- docs/plans/2026-03-06-linear-phase-3-completion-design.md
- docs/plans/2026-03-06-linear-phase-3-completion-plan.md

## Context
`auth-broker` still stores some Linear ownership scope in metadata/payload envelopes rather than first-class columns. That works for the current user/org fallback, but it makes team-scoped authz, autosync routing, and long-term observability unnecessarily fragile.

## Goals
- Promote `betterAuthOrganizationId` and `betterAuthTeamId` to first-class persisted fields for Linear connection and webhook delivery records.
- Preserve compatibility fallback for legacy rows during rollout.
- Keep the auth-broker service deployable in Railway's isolated Docker image.

## Notes
- This is the foundational data-model ticket for the remaining Linear phase-3 work.
- Should block team authz enforcement and autosync subscription work.

## Links

## Context
The macOS review queue currently stores review notes locally in Hack Desktop state. Conflict history and manual review decisions should travel with the repo just like other git-backed ticket sync state.

## Goals
- Add repo-shared append-only review-note ticket events.
- Keep review notes separate from synced ticket comments so they do not leak to Linear.
- Replace desktop-local Linear review notes with ticket-backed shared state.

## Notes
- Review notes are project-local reconciliation/audit data, not broker-owned integration state.
- This can proceed in parallel with broker ownership/authz work.
